We consider the curvature of a family of warped products of two pseduo-Riemannian manifolds $(B,g_B)$ and $(F,g_F)$ furnished with metrics of the form $c^{2}g_B \oplus w^2 g_F$ and, in particular, of the type $w^{2 \mu}g_B \oplus w^2 g_F$, where $c, w \colon B \to (0,\infty)$ are smooth functions and $\mu$ is a real parameter. We obtain suitable expressions for the Ricci tensor and scalar curvature of such products that allow us to establish results about the existence of Einstein or constant scalar curvature structures in these categories. If $(B,g_B)$ is Riemannian, the latter question involves nonlinear elliptic partial differential equations with concave-convex nonlinearities and singular partial differential equations of the Lichnerowicz-York type among others.

We study the curvature of warped products formed from two pseudo-Riemannian manifolds \((B,g_B)\) and \((F,g_F)\), equipped with metrics
\[
c^{2}g_B\oplus w^{2}g_F,
\]
with particular attention to metrics of the form
\[
w^{2\mu}g_B\oplus w^{2}g_F,
\]
where \(c,w:B\to(0,\infty)\) are smooth functions and \(\mu\in\mathbb{R}\). We derive formulas for the Ricci tensor and scalar curvature that can be used to investigate when these products admit Einstein metrics or metrics of constant scalar curvature. When \((B,g_B)\) is Riemannian, the constant-scalar-curvature problem leads, among other equations, to nonlinear elliptic PDEs featuring concave-convex nonlinearities and to singular PDEs of Lichnerowicz–York type.

The text investigates the curvature of warped products constructed from two pseudo-Riemannian manifolds, \((B,g_B)\) and \((F,g_F)\). It considers metrics on the product manifold \(B\times F\) of the form
\[
c^{2}g_B\oplus w^{2}g_F,
\]
where \(c\) and \(w\) are positive smooth functions defined on the base manifold \(B\). Particular attention is given to the family
\[
w^{2\mu}g_B\oplus w^{2}g_F,
\]
in which the conformal factor on the base is related to the warping function by a real parameter \(\mu\).

For these classes of warped metrics, explicit and useful formulas are derived for both the Ricci tensor and the scalar curvature. These formulas clarify how the geometry of the base and fiber, the functions \(c\) and \(w\), and their derivatives contribute to the curvature of the total product manifold.

The resulting curvature identities are then applied to geometric existence problems. In particular, they provide a framework for determining when such warped products admit Einstein metrics or metrics of constant scalar curvature. When the base \((B,g_B)\) is Riemannian, the constant scalar curvature condition can be reformulated as a nonlinear elliptic partial differential equation. Depending on the relevant dimensions and parameter values, the resulting equations exhibit concave-convex nonlinearities or take the form of singular Lichnerowicz–York-type equations. Thus, the geometric analysis of these warped products leads naturally to significant nonlinear elliptic problems.

Let \((B^{m},g_{B})\) and \((F^{k},g_{F})\) be pseudo-Riemannian manifolds, and consider on \(B\times F\) the metric  
\[
g=c^{2}g_{B}\oplus w^{2}g_{F},
\]
where \(c\) and \(w\) are positive smooth functions on the base. This construction combines a conformal deformation of the base with an ordinary warped product and includes, as an important special case, the one-function family
\[
g=w^{2\mu}g_{B}\oplus w^{2}g_{F},
\]
where \(\mu\in\mathbb{R}\). The curvature of these metrics is computed explicitly in terms of the Ricci tensors and scalar curvatures of the factors, together with the gradient, Hessian, and Laplacian of the warping functions. In particular, if \(h=c^{2}g_{B}\), then the Ricci tensor has no mixed components and satisfies
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_{g}(X,Y)
 =\operatorname{Ric}_{h}(X,Y)-k\,w^{-1}\operatorname{Hess}_{h}w(X,Y)
\]
for vectors tangent to \(B\), while for vectors tangent to \(F\),
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_{g}(U,V)
 =\operatorname{Ric}_{F}(U,V)
 -\bigl(w\Delta_{h}w+(k-1)|\nabla w|_{h}^{2}\bigr)g_{F}(U,V).
\]
Consequently,
\[
S_{g}
 =S_{h}+w^{-2}S_{F}
 -2k\,w^{-1}\Delta_{h}w
 -k(k-1)w^{-2}|\nabla w|_{h}^{2}.
\]
Combining these identities with the conformal-change formulas for \(h=c^{2}g_{B}\) gives expressions entirely in terms of \(g_{B}\), \(c\), and \(w\).

For the specialization \(c=w^{\mu}\), the curvature formulas simplify to differential equations involving a single positive function. Suitable changes of variable absorb the quadratic gradient terms and transform the scalar-curvature condition into a semilinear equation. The Einstein condition similarly reduces to a coupled system on the base, together with the requirement that the fiber be Einstein. These reductions make it possible to identify the parameter values for which the equations degenerate, to separate exceptional low-dimensional cases, and to derive criteria for the existence or nonexistence of Einstein and constant-scalar-curvature metrics in this class.

When the base is Riemannian, the resulting equations are elliptic. Depending on the dimensions, the parameter \(\mu\), and the prescribed scalar curvatures of the base, fiber, and total space, they take the form of nonlinear elliptic equations with competing concave and convex power nonlinearities. Standard variational, sub- and supersolution, and maximum-principle methods can therefore be applied under appropriate compactness and sign assumptions. In other parameter ranges, the reduction produces equations containing negative powers of the unknown function. These are singular semilinear equations of Lichnerowicz–York type, closely related to those arising in the conformal method for the Einstein constraint equations. Thus, the curvature calculations provide both a unified geometric description of conformal warped products and an analytic framework for constructing new pseudo-Riemannian Einstein and constant-scalar-curvature metrics.
outputs.L5:
## Riemannian Geometry, Ricci Curvature, and Einstein Manifolds

Riemannian geometry studies smooth spaces equipped with a **Riemannian metric**. This metric assigns an inner product to each tangent space, allowing geometric quantities such as lengths, angles, volumes, and geodesics to be defined on curved manifolds. It generalizes the familiar geometry of Euclidean space to surfaces and higher-dimensional spaces.

A central object in Riemannian geometry is the **Riemann curvature tensor**, which measures how a manifold bends. By taking a trace of this tensor, one obtains the **Ricci curvature tensor**. Ricci curvature describes how the volume of a small region differs from the corresponding volume in Euclidean space. It also plays an important role in geometric analysis, particularly in the Ricci flow equation introduced by Richard Hamilton:

\[
\frac{\partial g}{\partial t}=-2\,\mathrm{Ric}(g).
\]

This evolution equation deforms a Riemannian metric according to its Ricci curvature and was a key tool in Grigori Perelman’s proof of the Poincaré conjecture.

An **Einstein manifold** is a Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian manifold whose Ricci tensor is proportional to the metric:

\[
\mathrm{Ric}=\lambda g,
\]

where \(\lambda\) is a constant. Such manifolds have constant Ricci curvature, although their full curvature need not be constant. Depending on the sign of \(\lambda\), an Einstein manifold may have positive, zero, or negative Ricci curvature. Spheres, Euclidean spaces, and hyperbolic spaces are standard examples.

The term “Einstein” reflects the connection with Albert Einstein’s theory of general relativity. In that theory, spacetime is modeled by a pseudo-Riemannian manifold, and its geometry is governed by the Einstein field equations:

\[
\mathrm{Ric}-\frac{1}{2}Rg+\Lambda g
=
\frac{8\pi G}{c^4}T.
\]

Here \(R\) is the scalar curvature, \(\Lambda\) is the cosmological constant, and \(T\) represents matter and energy. Thus, Ricci curvature provides a fundamental bridge between abstract Riemannian geometry and the physical description of gravity.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize research on Ricci tensors, scalar curvature, Einstein metrics, and constant scalar curvature structures for conformally warped pseudo-Riemannian products.
counterfactuals.output:
## Overview

A **conformally warped pseudo-Riemannian product** is typically a product manifold
\[
M=B^n\times F^m
\]
equipped with
\[
\bar g=e^{2u}g,\qquad  
g=g_B+f^2g_F,
\]
where \(f>0\) is the warping function and \(u\) is the conformal factor. Both may be restricted to the base \(B\), although more general work allows dependence on both factors. The signatures of \(g_B\) and \(g_F\) are arbitrary.

Research in this area combines the curvature formulas for warped products with conformal-change formulas. The main objectives are to classify Einstein metrics, construct constant-scalar-curvature metrics, and derive rigidity or nonexistence results under completeness, compactness, or symmetry assumptions.

## Fundamental curvature formulas

Let \(N=n+m\), and use the convention \(\Delta=\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Hess}\). For the warped metric
\[
g=g_B+f^2g_F,
\]
its Ricci tensor satisfies, for \(X,Y\in TB\) and \(U,V\in TF\),
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_g(X,Y)
=
\operatorname{Ric}_B(X,Y)-m f^{-1}\operatorname{Hess}_B f(X,Y),
\]
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_g(X,U)=0,
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_g(U,V)
=
\operatorname{Ric}_F(U,V)
-
\bigl(f\Delta_B f+(m-1)|\nabla f|_B^2\bigr)g_F(U,V).
\]

Consequently,
\[
R_g
=
R_B+f^{-2}R_F
-2m f^{-1}\Delta_B f
-m(m-1)f^{-2}|\nabla f|_B^2.
\]

These formulas remain valid in arbitrary signature, with all traces and squared norms interpreted pseudo-Riemannianly. In particular, \(|\nabla f|^2\) can be positive, negative, or zero without \(\nabla f\) vanishing.

Under the conformal change \(\bar g=e^{2u}g\),
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_{\bar g}
=
\operatorname{Ric}_g
-(N-2)(\operatorname{Hess}_g u-du\otimes du)
-\bigl(\Delta_g u+(N-2)|\nabla u|_g^2\bigr)g,
\]
and
\[
R_{\bar g}
=
e^{-2u}\left[
R_g-2(N-1)\Delta_g u
-(N-1)(N-2)|\nabla u|_g^2
\right].
\]

Thus nearly all classification problems reduce to a coupled system involving \(f\), \(u\), and the curvature of the two factors.

## Einstein metrics

The Einstein condition
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_{\bar g}=\lambda \bar g
\]
splits into base, fiber, and mixed equations.

When both \(f\) and \(u\) depend only on \(B\), the mixed Ricci components vanish automatically. Moreover,
\[
\Delta_g u=\Delta_Bu+m f^{-1}\langle\nabla f,\nabla u\rangle_B,
\]
while the vertical Hessian is
\[
\operatorname{Hess}_g u(U,V)
=
f\langle\nabla f,\nabla u\rangle_B\,g_F(U,V).
\]

The fiber equation then forces \(F\) to be Einstein in most nondegenerate cases:
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_F=\mu g_F
\]
for a constant \(\mu\). The base equation becomes a nonlinear tensor equation containing
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_B,\quad
f^{-1}\operatorname{Hess}f,\quad
\operatorname{Hess}u,\quad
du\otimes du,
\]
plus gradient interactions between \(f\) and \(u\).

A useful simplification is to absorb the conformal factor into a change of variables. For instance,
\[
e^{2u}(g_B+f^2g_F)
=
(e^{2u}g_B)+(e^u f)^2g_F.
\]
If \(u\) is base-dependent, the metric is itself a warped product with new base metric \(e^{2u}g_B\) and new warping function \(e^u f\). This observation explains why many results can be reformulated using standard warped-product Einstein equations, quasi-Einstein metrics, or Bakry–Émery-type tensors.

Common conclusions in the literature include:

- the fiber must be Einstein;
- compact or complete Riemannian bases often force one of the factors \(f\) or \(u\) to be constant under sign assumptions;
- low-dimensional or cohomogeneity-one settings reduce the Einstein system to ODEs;
- nontrivial examples are more abundant in indefinite signature because null gradients invalidate several positive-definite maximum-principle arguments;
- if \(u\) depends on both factors, the mixed Einstein equations impose strong separability conditions and often force \(u\) to split additively or the warping to become trivial.

## Constant scalar curvature

For prescribed constant scalar curvature \(R_{\bar g}=\Lambda\), one obtains
\[
R_g-2(N-1)\Delta_g u
-(N-1)(N-2)|\nabla u|_g^2
=
\Lambda e^{2u}.
\]

For \(N\ge3\), writing
\[
\bar g=v^{4/(N-2)}g
\]
converts this into the Yamabe-type equation
\[
-\frac{4(N-1)}{N-2}\Delta_g v+R_gv
=
\Lambda v^{(N+2)/(N-2)}.
\]

Substitution of the warped scalar-curvature formula gives a nonlinear equation coupling \(v\) and \(f\):
\[
-\frac{4(N-1)}{N-2}\Delta_g v
+
\left(
R_B+f^{-2}R_F
-2m f^{-1}\Delta_B f
-m(m-1)f^{-2}|\nabla f|^2
\right)v
=
\Lambda v^{(N+2)/(N-2)}.
\]

When \(v\) is base-dependent,
\[
\Delta_gv=\Delta_Bv+m f^{-1}\langle\nabla f,\nabla v\rangle_B,
\]
so the problem reduces to a weighted semilinear equation on \(B\). This weighted formulation is central to existence and uniqueness studies.

In Riemannian signature, variational methods, Sobolev inequalities, maximum principles, and the Yamabe functional are available. In indefinite signature the operator is generally hyperbolic or ultrahyperbolic rather than elliptic, so the classical Yamabe theory does not transfer directly. Research there relies more heavily on symmetry reduction, local PDE theory, explicit ansätze, and causal or global-hyperbolic assumptions.

## Main research directions

1. **Classification and rigidity:** Determining when Einstein or constant-scalar-curvature conditions force \(f\), \(u\), or one factor metric to be trivial.

2. **Quasi-Einstein correspondence:** Base equations for Einstein warped products are closely related to \(m\)-quasi-Einstein and weighted Ricci curvature equations.

3. **Explicit constructions:** One-dimensional bases, radial conformal factors, Robertson–Walker-type metrics, static spacetimes, and fibers of constant sectional curvature yield solvable ODE systems.

4. **Compactness and completeness:** In the Riemannian setting, integration and maximum-principle arguments give strong obstructions. Indefinite signature admits additional complete and nontrivial solutions, especially with null dependence.

5. **Prescribed curvature problems:** Researchers study which functions can occur as scalar curvature within a conformally warped class and how the answer depends on fiber curvature and the spectrum of weighted Laplacians.

6. **Generalizations:** Multiply warped products, twisted products, gradient Ricci solitons, Einstein–matter equations, and metrics with density use essentially the same curvature decomposition.

## Overall conclusion

The curvature theory is algebraically well understood: Ricci and scalar curvature follow by combining the Bishop–O’Neill warped-product identities with standard conformal transformation laws. The difficult research questions are analytical and global—solving the resulting coupled nonlinear PDEs, determining completeness, and proving rigidity. In positive-definite signature, compactness and ellipticity often produce strong classification theorems; in pseudo-Riemannian signature, null directions and nonelliptic operators permit a wider range of local and global geometries but make general existence theory substantially harder.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a journal-style abstract explaining how curvature formulas for warped products lead to nonlinear elliptic PDEs with concave-convex nonlinearities and Lichnerowicz–York-type singular equations.
counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract.** We examine how prescribed-curvature problems on warped products generate nonlinear elliptic equations with competing power-law nonlinearities. For a warped metric \(g=g_B+f^{2}g_F\) on \(B\times F\), the scalar-curvature identity
\[
R_g=R_B+f^{-2}R_F-2m f^{-1}\Delta_B f-m(m-1)f^{-2}|\nabla f|^2,
\]
where \(m=\dim F\), converts geometric curvature constraints into semilinear equations on the base. A suitable power substitution \(f=u^\alpha\) removes the quadratic gradient term and produces equations of the form
\[
-\Delta_Bu+a(x)u=b(x)u^{p}+c(x)u^{q},
\qquad 0<p<1<q,
\]
exhibiting the characteristic concave–convex interaction. When additional curvature, constraint, or matter terms scale with negative powers of the warping factor, the same reduction yields singular equations
\[
-\Delta_Bu+a(x)u=b(x)u^{q}+d(x)u^{-r},
\qquad r>0,
\]
of Lichnerowicz–York type. Thus warped-product curvature formulas provide a direct geometric mechanism for both sublinear–superlinear competition and inverse-power singularities. The resulting correspondence links the geometry of prescribed scalar curvature and Einstein-type constraints with variational, sub- and supersolution, and bifurcation methods for nonlinear elliptic PDEs.

counterfactuals.prompt: What are the main geometric and PDE consequences of studying warped-product metrics of the form \(c^2g_B \oplus w^2g_F\) on \(B\times F\)?
counterfactuals.output:
Assume \(B^m\) and \(F^n\) are Riemannian, and \(c,w>0\) are functions on \(B\). Set
\[
G=c^2g_B\oplus w^2g_F=h\oplus w^2g_F,\qquad h=c^2g_B.
\]
Thus the construction is an ordinary warped product with conformally changed base metric \(h\).

## Geometric consequences

- **Horizontal–vertical splitting:** \(TB\) and \(TF\) are orthogonal, and all mixed Ricci components vanish.
- **Fibers are totally umbilic:** each \(\{b\}\times F\) has induced metric \(w(b)^2g_F\), with mean curvature determined by
  \[
  -n\,\nabla_h\log w.
  \]
  They are totally geodesic exactly when \(w\) is constant.
- **Volume form:**
  \[
  d\mu_G=c^m w^n\,d\mu_{g_B}\,d\mu_{g_F}.
  \]
- **Curvature splits into base, fiber, and mixed terms.** In particular,
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}_G|_{TB}
  =\operatorname{Ric}_h-nw^{-1}\operatorname{Hess}_h w,
  \]
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}_G|_{TF}
  =\operatorname{Ric}_F-
  \bigl(w\Delta_h w+(n-1)|\nabla w|_h^2\bigr)g_F,
  \]
  and
  \[
  R_G=R_h+w^{-2}R_F
  -2n\,w^{-1}\Delta_h w
  -n(n-1)w^{-2}|\nabla w|_h^2.
  \]
  Mixed sectional curvature is controlled by \(-w^{-1}\operatorname{Hess}_h w\), while vertical sectional curvature contains the correction \(-|\nabla w|_h^2/w^2\).

The conformal factor \(c\) contributes through the usual conformal formulas. Writing \(u=\log c\),
\[
R_h=c^{-2}\!\left[
R_{g_B}-2(m-1)\Delta_{g_B}u
-(m-1)(m-2)|\nabla u|_{g_B}^2
\right],
\]
and
\[
\Delta_h w=c^{-2}\bigl(\Delta_{g_B}w
 +(m-2)\langle\nabla u,\nabla w\rangle_{g_B}\bigr).
\]

## PDE consequences

Curvature conditions on \(G\) reduce to differential equations on the lower-dimensional base \(B\):

- **Einstein metrics:** \(\operatorname{Ric}_G=\lambda G\) becomes
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}_h-nw^{-1}\operatorname{Hess}_h w=\lambda h,
  \]
  together with
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}_F=
  \bigl(w\Delta_h w+(n-1)|\nabla w|_h^2+\lambda w^2\bigr)g_F.
  \]
  Hence, except in degenerate cases, \(F\) must itself be Einstein, and \(c,w\) satisfy a coupled nonlinear elliptic system on \(B\).

- **Constant scalar curvature/Yamabe problems:** prescribing \(R_G\) gives a semilinear or quasilinear elliptic equation involving \(c,w,\Delta c,\Delta w\), and their gradient interactions.

- **Other geometric equations**—Ricci solitons, quasi-Einstein metrics, static vacuum equations, prescribed Ricci curvature—similarly become weighted Hessian equations on \(B\). Warped Einstein metrics are closely related to \(n\)-quasi-Einstein structures:
  \[
  \operatorname{Ric}_h+\operatorname{Hess}\phi-\frac1n\,d\phi\otimes d\phi
  =\lambda h,\qquad \phi=-n\log w.
  \]

- **Analytic tools become available:** on a compact base, integration identities, maximum principles, and Bochner formulas often force rigidity—for example, constancy of \(w\) under suitable curvature or sign assumptions. The natural weighted measure is
  \[
  w^n\,d\mu_h=c^m w^n\,d\mu_{g_B}.
  \]

Overall, the ansatz converts a high-dimensional geometric problem on \(B\times F\) into a coupled system for two positive scalar functions on \(B\), while retaining explicit control of curvature, volume, completeness, and fiber geometry. If \(c\) or \(w\) are allowed to depend on \(F\) as well, this clean warped-product reduction generally breaks down and mixed curvature/PDE terms appear.

counterfactuals.prompt: Produce a brief technical overview of a paper analyzing the family \(w^{2\mu}g_B\oplus w^2g_F\), including formulas for Ricci and scalar curvature and applications to Einstein and constant-scalar-curvature metrics.
counterfactuals.output:
### Technical overview

The paper studies **base-conformal warped products**
\[
(M,g)=\bigl(B^m\times F^k,\; g=w^{2\mu}g_B\oplus w^2g_F\bigr),
\]
where \(w>0\) is a smooth function on \(B\), \(\mu\in\mathbb R\), and \(m=\dim B\), \(k=\dim F\). This family interpolates between ordinary warped products (\(\mu=0\)) and metrics conformal to a direct product (\(\mu=1\)).

All derivatives below are taken with respect to \(g_B\), with \(\Delta=\operatorname{div}\nabla\). Define
\[
A=(m-1)\mu+k.
\]

For horizontal vectors \(X,Y\in TB\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Ric}_g(X,Y)
={}&\operatorname{Ric}_B(X,Y)
-\bigl((m-2)\mu+k\bigr)\frac{\operatorname{Hess}w(X,Y)}{w}\\
&+\mu\bigl((m-2)(\mu+1)+2k\bigr)
 \frac{dw(X)dw(Y)}{w^2}\\
&-\mu\frac{\Delta w}{w}\,g_B(X,Y)
+\mu\bigl(1-k-(m-2)\mu\bigr)
 \frac{|\nabla w|^2}{w^2}\,g_B(X,Y).
\end{aligned}
\]

For vertical vectors \(U,V\in TF\),
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_g(U,V)
=
\operatorname{Ric}_F(U,V)
-
\left[
w^{1-2\mu}\Delta w+
\bigl((m-2)\mu+k-1\bigr)w^{-2\mu}|\nabla w|^2
\right]g_F(U,V),
\]
and the mixed Ricci components vanish.

The scalar curvature is
\[
R_g
=
w^{-2\mu}
\left[
R_B
-2A\frac{\Delta w}{w}
-C\frac{|\nabla w|^2}{w^2}
\right]
+w^{-2}R_F,
\]
where
\[
C=(m-1)(m-2)\mu^2
+2\bigl(k(m-2)-(m-1)\bigr)\mu
+k(k-1).
\]

### Einstein metrics

If \(g_F\) is Einstein, \(\operatorname{Ric}_F=\nu g_F\), then \(g\) is Einstein with constant \(\lambda\) precisely when the horizontal tensor equation
\[
\operatorname{Ric}_g|_{TB}=\lambda w^{2\mu}g_B
\]
holds together with the scalar fiber equation
\[
\nu-
w^{1-2\mu}\Delta w
-\bigl((m-2)\mu+k-1\bigr)w^{-2\mu}|\nabla w|^2
=\lambda w^2.
\]
Thus the Einstein problem reduces to an overdetermined Hessian equation on \(B\) plus a semilinear equation for \(w\). Tracing and combining these equations gives rigidity and existence criteria, especially when \(B\) or \(F\) is already Einstein.

### Constant scalar curvature

Prescribing \(R_g=\rho\) yields
\[
R_B
-2A\frac{\Delta w}{w}
-C\frac{|\nabla w|^2}{w^2}
+R_F w^{2\mu-2}
=\rho\,w^{2\mu}.
\]
For \(A\neq0\), a power substitution \(u=w^\alpha\), with \(\alpha\) chosen to absorb the quadratic gradient term, converts this into a Yamabe-type semilinear elliptic equation. The exceptional value
\[
\mu=-\frac{k}{m-1}
\]
makes \(A=0\), eliminating the Laplacian term from the scalar-curvature formula and requiring separate treatment. These reductions provide constructions and nonexistence results for Einstein and constant-scalar-curvature metrics within the family.
